LESSON: TURNING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.4: Turning
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Turning, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is turning an important skill for a player during a game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to turning for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Turning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the different directions of turning in movement,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Turning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform turning in different directions for coordination,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Turning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate turning as a basic skill for body movement during play. • in purposive groups, the learners are guided to observe and sign words related to turning such as direction— (left, right, half, full and combinatio

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Turning together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner creatively performs turning in different directions.

• Communication and Collaboration: The learner talks about or signs various directions of turning while demonstrating.

Values:
• Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions while discussing various directions the body turns.

• Unity: The learner cooperates with others as they work in groups to perform turning in different directions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness and self-esteem: The learner displays confidence as they turn in different directions.

15

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics Activities: The learner learns directions and patterns.

Suggested learning resources.

Compass, whistles, flags for signals.
